findings.message: The GitHub accounts card now pins `list_secrets {}`, the list of every connector credential. The card shows one record: whether the `github-oauth` app is set up. The old pin pointed at the right record but threw an error when the credential was missing. The new pin answers in both states, but it resolves to a different, wider record, labelled "Connector credentials" instead of the card. This is the same pattern as the earlier lesson where a hub card was pinned to `settings_overview`. Fix: add a read that answers for this one connector in both states (for example `get_secret_meta` returning `{ connector, status: 'not configured' }` instead of not-found, or a git-accounts read `get_github_app_status`), and pin that with the card's own label.
findings.scenario: An Admin pins the GitHub accounts card on a tenant with Xero and GitHub push credentials and asks 'why isn't this set up?' → chat receives the metadata of every credential (xero, github…), labelled 'Connector credentials', not the github-oauth status the card shows.

findings.message: This round fixed the check-then-insert race for emails only: `linked` is now read back from the insert. The login has the same race. `loginTaken` comes from a SELECT, and since 0033 dropped `unique (tenant_id, provider, login)`, no index stops two people from holding the same login. `git_identity_login_email` includes the email, so rows with different emails, or a login-only row, don't conflict. `linkGitIdentity` (delivery's suggestion accept) uses the same unguarded check. Fix: add a constraint that a (tenant, provider, lower(login)) belongs to one user. For example, take `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(tenant||provider||lower(login)))` in both writers before the check, or keep a per-login owner table with a unique key. Add a two-writer race test for the login, as was done for the email.
findings.scenario: An Admin accepts delivery's suggestion linking `kasun-dias` (no email) to Nimal while Kasun finishes connecting `kasun-dias`. Both checks see no other holder, and both inserts succeed. `kasun-dias` now belongs to two people, and `findGitIdentity` (limit 1, no tiebreak by user) attributes Kasun's commits and proposals to either one.

findings.message: The previous round's two fixes covered the Disconnect card only. Reconnecting has the same effects. `setGitHubIdentities` deletes every github row of the person that isn't the returned login plus its kept emails. That removes the person's other logins (for example `@kasun-old`) and any email GitHub no longer lists. The README says a reconnect that drops an email loses ownership at the next sync. Yet the Connect card says only '@a, @b: connecting again replaces their emails'. It doesn't say that other logins are removed, and it has no OWNERS_NOTE. Fix: the connect card should say that logins and emails GitHub doesn't return are removed, and carry the owners note, so it matches the README.
findings.scenario: Kasun holds @kasun-dias and @kasun-old (from a delivery suggestion) and confirms Connect GitHub, then approves on GitHub as @kasun-dias → the @kasun-old row is deleted, and proposals matched through it become unowned at the next sync. The card he confirmed said nothing of either.

findings.message: The connect is now three steps: claim, read GitHub, store. `withdrawSuggestions` runs after `storeConnect` has committed, in its own transaction. If it throws, the callback falls into the unknown-error branch and tells the person 'something went wrong; try again', although their identities are stored. A retry with the same link is refused as 'expired or already used'. A new connect does not withdraw the stale suggestion if nothing new is linked (`r.linked.length` is 0 when the rows already exist? no: they are re-inserted, but the earlier failure state is the same each time). The open `delivery.git-identity` suggestion stays, and accepting it then fails. Fix: run the withdraw inside storeConnect's transaction (pass tx), or catch and log its failure separately and still report the connect as done.
findings.scenario: The agents' withdraw fails (DB error or a permission error on the job context) after storeConnect commits → the page shows 'GitHub: failed, something went wrong; try again', while auth.git_identity holds the new rows and the link suggestion stays open for an Admin.

findings.message: The B12 fix (a 10-second timeout on every GitHub call, and no GitHub call inside a write) has no test. The new table covers only schema mismatches and a refused code. No case has the fake GitHub hang or close the connection, and none checks that the claim is not held open by a transaction while GitHub is read. Fix: add cases to the fake GitHub (a code whose /user never answers, and one that resets the socket). Assert that completeGitHubConnect rejects with GitHubReplyError within the timeout (shorten it through an injectable value in the test), that nothing is stored, and that no transaction is open while GitHub is called (for example, the connect_state row can be updated by another session meanwhile).
findings.scenario: Remove `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(TIMEOUT_MS)` from `call()` → every test still passes, and a hung /user leaves the callback request open with no limit.

findings.message: The comment says ties keep 'the oldest row', but the order uses `ctid`. ctid is a physical row position, which UPDATE and VACUUM FULL change, so it is not creation order (the table has no created_at). The dropped rows are recorded only as `raise notice`, which most migration runners discard, so the person whose identity was dropped can't be found afterwards. Fix: fix the comment, or order by something stable. Write the dropped rows to a durable place (for example an audit row or a `core.migration_note` table) rather than a notice only.
findings.scenario: Two people's rows share an email, neither verified, and the newer row was physically written earlier after a VACUUM FULL → the newer row is kept, contrary to the comment, and the drop is visible only in a discarded NOTICE.
